lessons.title: Contrast, alignment and hierarchy: the three rules that fix most designs
objectives: Explain contrast, alignment, hierarchy, repetition, proximity and white space in plain words
Spot the three most common mistakes in a busy flyer
Redesign a cluttered flyer so the main message is read first
Check text contrast so it can be read on a small phone screen

blocks.text: Most people who say "I am not creative" are really saying "nobody showed me the rules". Good design is mostly a set of simple rules that professional designers apply again and again. In this lesson you learn six of them. Three of them, **contrast, alignment and hierarchy**, will fix most of the flyers you see on WhatsApp statuses and church notice boards.

blocks.name: design-thinking
blocks.alt: A woman thinking through a design layout
blocks.caption: Design is a set of choices you can learn, not a gift you are born with.

blocks.text: Rule 1: Hierarchy, decide what is read first

**Hierarchy** means arranging things so the eye reads them in the order you want. The most important thing should be the biggest, boldest or most colourful. The second most important thing is smaller. Small details, such as a phone number or address, come last and smallest. If everything is the same size, the viewer does not know where to start, so she scrolls past.

A useful habit: before you open Canva, write your message in three levels on paper. Level 1 is the hook ("Fresh Zobo, 500 naira"). Level 2 is the support ("Chilled, no preservatives, delivery in Ikeja"). Level 3 is the action ("WhatsApp 0803 000 0000"). Each level then gets its own size.
Rule 2: Contrast, make it readable

**Contrast** is the difference between two things: dark against light, big against small, bold against thin. Text must contrast strongly with its background. Yellow text on a white background, or dark blue text on a black background, disappears on a phone screen, especially outdoors in bright sunlight. The international web accessibility guideline (WCAG) asks for a contrast ratio of at least **4.5 to 1** for normal text and **3 to 1** for large text. You do not need to calculate it: free tools such as the WebAIM contrast checker do it for you, and the simple test is to squint. If the words blur into the background when you squint, the contrast is too low.
Rule 3: Alignment, line things up

**Alignment** means every item lines up with something else: the left edge, the centre line, or another block of text. Randomly placed text looks amateur even when the colours are beautiful. Canva helps you here: when you drag an item, thin pink or purple guide lines appear when it lines up with the centre or with another element. Pick one alignment for a design (all left, or all centred) and stick to it. Left alignment is easier to read for more than two lines.
Rules 4 to 6: Repetition, proximity and white space

items: **Repetition**: use the same two fonts and the same colours across all your posts so people recognise you before they read your name.
**Proximity**: keep related things close together. Price next to product name. Date, time and venue grouped in one block.

**White space**: the empty space around items. It is not wasted. It gives the eye a rest and makes the main message stand out. A good rule is to keep at least a thumb's width of margin around the edge of a phone design.

blocks.title: Three levels of hierarchy
items: Hook: biggest, boldest
Support: medium size
Action: small, clear
blocks.caption: Every design should have one clear top level, a supporting middle and a small call to action at the base.

What it looks like
Fix

blocks.title: Worked example: fixing a crowded event flyer
blocks.context: For example, Bisi in Ibadan made a flyer for her women's group meeting. It had seven lines of text in four fonts, a full photo background, and the date hidden at the bottom in small yellow letters.
steps: She writes the three levels: Hook "Women in Business Meetup", Support "Saturday 14 June, 10am, Community Hall, Bodija", Action "Free entry. RSVP on WhatsApp 0805 000 0000".
She cuts the remaining lines (the long prayer and the list of sponsors) and moves them into the WhatsApp caption instead.
She keeps one bold heading font at about 90 points and one simple body font at about 36 points.
She places a dark green rectangle at 80% transparency over the photo so white text has strong contrast.
She left aligns all text to the same margin and leaves space between the three blocks.
blocks.result: The new flyer has three clear blocks. When she shows it to her sister for three seconds, her sister can repeat the event name and date, which the old flyer failed.

blocks.title: The three-second test
blocks.text: Show your design to someone for three seconds, then hide it. Ask what it was about. If she cannot tell you the main message, your hierarchy or contrast needs work.

takeaways: Hierarchy decides what is read first: one hook, one support block, one action.
Strong contrast between text and background is essential on small phone screens.
Line everything up and keep related items close together.
Use white space and margins; empty space is part of the design.

activity.title: Redesign a flyer you have seen
steps: Screenshot a busy flyer from a WhatsApp status or group (keep it private, it is only for practice).
On paper, write its message in three levels: hook, support, action.
List every mistake you see using the table in this lesson.
Sketch a better layout by hand, showing where each level goes and how big it is.
Do the three-second test with a friend on both versions.
activity.evidence: The original screenshot, your three-level message and your sketch, saved together in one phone album.

lessons.title: Building your brand look: colours, fonts and a simple logo
objectives: Choose a three to five colour brand palette with HEX codes
Pair a heading font with a body font that are easy to read
Create a simple text logo you are allowed to own
Write a one-page brand guide for your business or group

blocks.text: A **brand visual identity** is the set of colours, fonts, logo and photo style that makes people recognise your business before they read your name. Big companies spend a lot on it, but a small business can build a clean one in an afternoon with a phone. The goal is **consistency**: the same look on your flyers, Instagram posts, WhatsApp catalogue, price list and shop sign.

blocks.name: color-palette
blocks.alt: A person choosing colours from a palette
blocks.caption: A small, fixed palette makes every post look like it came from the same business.

blocks.text: Step 1: Decide how you want people to feel

Write three words that describe your business personality. A children's tutoring centre might choose "playful, safe, bright". A bridal makeup artist might choose "elegant, soft, premium". A catering business might choose "warm, generous, fresh". These words guide every colour and font choice that follows.
Step 2: Build a palette with HEX codes

Every digital colour has a **HEX code**: a hash sign followed by six letters and numbers, such as #D4006A for a deep magenta. HEX codes let you use exactly the same colour in Canva, CapCut and anywhere else. A practical small palette has:

items: **One main colour** that people will remember you by.
**One accent colour** for buttons, prices and highlights. It should contrast clearly with the main colour.
**One dark neutral** (near black or dark grey) for body text.
**One light neutral** (white, cream or very light grey) for backgrounds.
Optionally, one extra supporting colour.

blocks.text: Canva has a free colour palette generator on its website, and inside the editor you can tap any colour swatch and type a HEX code. If you already have a logo or a product photo you love, upload it: Canva will show the colours used in that photo under **Photo colours**, and you can copy them.
Step 3: Pair two fonts

Fonts come in families. **Serif** fonts have small feet at the ends of letters (like Playfair Display) and feel classic. **Sans serif** fonts have no feet (like Montserrat or Open Sans) and are very clear on screens. **Script** fonts look like handwriting and are hard to read in long text. A safe pairing is a strong heading font plus a plain sans serif body font. Use script fonts only for one or two decorative words, never for phone numbers or prices.
All the fonts in this table are free Google Fonts and are available in Canva's font list.

Two practical font rules for phone screens: body text on a 1080 pixel wide post should rarely be smaller than about 28 to 32 points in Canva, or it becomes hard to read on a small phone; and never use more than two font families in one design. You can still vary weight (regular, bold) and size inside those two families to create hierarchy.
Step 5: Decide your photo style

Your photos are part of your brand too. Decide a simple rule and keep to it, for example "bright daylight photos on a plain cream background" or "people using the product, outdoors, warm light". Mixing dark, yellow-tinted night photos with bright daylight ones makes a feed look untidy even when the colours and fonts match.
Step 4: A simple logo you can own

For most small businesses, a clean **wordmark** (your business name set in your heading font, in your main colour, maybe with one simple shape) is enough. Be careful: Canva's content licence does not allow you to register a trademark for a logo built from Canva's stock graphics or templates, because those elements are not exclusively yours. If you may ever want to register your brand, build the logo from text and basic shapes only, or hire a designer to create original artwork.

blocks.caption: Each step builds on the one before, so your choices stay consistent.

blocks.title: Worked example: a brand look for a small catering business
blocks.context: For example, Amaka runs a home catering business in Enugu called "Amaka's Pot". She sells party jollof and small chops and posts on WhatsApp Status and Instagram.
steps: Personality words: warm, generous, fresh.
Palette: main tomato red #C8102E, accent golden yellow #F2A900, dark text #222222, light background #FFF8EE.
Fonts: Poppins SemiBold for headings, Nunito for body text.
Logo: "Amaka's Pot" in Poppins SemiBold, red, with a simple yellow circle behind the A, made from a basic Canva shape.
She writes all of this on one Canva page titled "Brand guide" and saves it as a PDF and an image in her phone gallery.
blocks.result: Every new flyer now starts from the brand guide. Customers begin to recognise the red and yellow posts in their status feed before reading the name.

blocks.title: Keep it written down
blocks.text: Your brand guide only works if you and anyone helping you can find it. Save the HEX codes and font names as a pinned note on your phone as well as in Canva.

takeaways: Consistency is the whole point of a brand look.
Use three to five colours and record their HEX codes.
Pair one heading font with one plain body font; keep script fonts for decoration only.
Build a logo from text and basic shapes if you may want to trademark it.

activity.title: Create your one-page brand guide
steps: Write three personality words for your business or group.
Choose a main, accent, dark and light colour and note their HEX codes.
Pick a heading font and a body font from the table or Canva's list.
Make a simple wordmark logo in Canva using text and one basic shape.
Put everything on one page titled "Brand guide" and download it.
activity.evidence: Your downloaded one-page brand guide (PNG or PDF) with HEX codes and font names visible.

lessons.title: Canva on your phone: the core skills
objectives: Find your way around the Canva mobile app home screen and editor
Start a design at the correct size and edit a template
Add and edit text, photos, elements and backgrounds
Download a design in the right file format for its use

blocks.text: **Canva** is a free design app for Android, iPhone and the web. The free plan includes thousands of templates, photos, graphics and fonts. **Canva Pro** is the paid plan; Pro items are marked with a small crown icon. Everything in this lesson works on the free plan. Canva also offers free premium access to eligible registered non profit organisations through its Canva for Nonprofits programme.

blocks.name: mobile-phone
blocks.caption: Everything in this lesson is done on the Canva mobile app.

blocks.text: Getting set up

items: Install Canva from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Check the developer is Canva.
Sign up with your email or Google account and confirm your email.
On the home screen, notice the search bar at the top, the purple **+** button to create a design, and the **Projects** tab where your saved designs live.

blocks.text: Start at the right size

Tap **+** and choose a design type such as Instagram Post, Your Story, Flyer or Facebook Post. Each one opens a blank page at the correct pixel size. You can also tap **Custom size** and type the width and height. Starting at the right size matters: stretching a square post into a story later leaves gaps or cuts off text.
The editor in five parts

head: Part of the screen
What it does
rows: Your design. Tap an item to select it; pinch to zoom.
Add elements, text, uploads, photos, templates and more using the **+** button
Options for that item: font, colour, effects, transparency, position, animate
Undo and redo arrows, and the share or download button
Add a page, duplicate a page, or reorder pages for carousels

blocks.text: Core actions you will use every day

items: **Edit text**: double tap a text box, type, then use Font, Font size and Colour from the toolbar. Use **Effects** for a shadow or a background behind text.
**Add your photo**: tap **+**, then **Gallery** or **Uploads**, and pick from your phone. Tap a photo frame in a template and choose **Replace** to drop your photo in.
**Elements**: search for shapes, lines, icons and frames. Free items have no crown.
**Background colour**: tap an empty part of the page, then tap the colour square and type your HEX code.
**Position and layers**: select an item, tap **Position** to move it forward, backward or align it to the page.
**Transparency**: the checkerboard icon makes an item see through, useful for text boxes over photos.

blocks.title: Canva design workflow
items: Choose design size
Pick template or blank
Replace text and photos
Apply brand colours
Download and share
blocks.caption: Follow the same five steps for every design and you will work faster.

blocks.text: Downloading the right file

head: File type
Best for
rows: Graphics with text, logos, flyers for WhatsApp and Instagram: sharp edges
Photo-heavy designs: smaller file size, saves data
Anything going to a printer: menus, banners, business cards

blocks.text: Before you download, tap the download button and look at the options. You can choose which pages to download (useful for a carousel of several pages), and for PNG on Pro you can choose a transparent background, useful for a logo. If a design looks blurred on WhatsApp, the usual cause is a low-quality photo inside it, not the download setting, so start with sharp photos.
Undo, copies and safety nets

Canva saves automatically while you are online. Still, tap the undo arrow freely while experimenting; it will step back through your recent changes. Before making big changes to a design you like, make a copy first from the Projects tab, so the original is never lost.

blocks.title: Worked example: a price list post from a template
blocks.context: For example, Halima sells fabrics in Kano and wants a square post listing her new Ankara prices.
steps: She taps **+**, chooses Instagram Post (1080 x 1080 pixels), and searches templates for "price list".
She picks a free template with a clean list layout and taps **Customise this template**.
She replaces the heading with "New Ankara Arrivals", and types three lines: 6 yards, 9,000 naira; 12 yards, 17,500 naira; Half piece, 4,800 naira (approximate prices for the example).
She taps the background, types her brand colour #1B4D3E, and changes the text to white for contrast.
She taps **Replace** on the photo frame and drops in a photo of her best selling fabric.
She downloads as PNG and shares straight to WhatsApp Status from the share menu.
blocks.result: In under 15 minutes she has a clean, branded price post. Because the design is saved in Projects, next month she only changes the prices.

blocks.title: Fonts in other languages
blocks.text: If you write in Yoruba or Igbo with tone marks, check that your chosen font shows every accented letter correctly. Some decorative fonts drop them; plain fonts such as Open Sans or Noto Sans usually handle them well.

blocks.title: Save data while designing
blocks.text: Canva needs internet. Design on Wi-Fi when you can, avoid scrolling endless templates, and download PNG or JPG rather than video when a still image will do.

takeaways: Always start a design at the correct size for where it will be posted.
Crown icons mean Canva Pro; everything else is free to use.
Replace template text and photos rather than designing from nothing.
Download PNG for text graphics, JPG for photos, PDF Print for printing, MP4 for motion.

activity.title: Make your first branded post
steps: Open Canva, tap +, and choose Instagram Post.
Pick a free template related to your business.
Replace all text with your own words and one photo with your own photo.
Change the background and text colours to your brand HEX codes.
Download as PNG and save it to a phone album called Content Course.
activity.evidence: The downloaded PNG of your first post plus a screenshot of it in your Canva Projects list.

lessons.title: Working faster in Canva: brand kit, reusable templates and resizing
objectives: Store brand colours and fonts so they are one tap away
Turn one good design into a reusable template for a series
Resize a design for different platforms without breaking it
Remove backgrounds and organise designs into folders

blocks.text: Once you know the basics, speed becomes your next goal. A small business owner does not have hours to design every post. In this lesson you set up Canva so that your brand look is built in, and you create a few **master designs** you can reuse every week.

blocks.name: design-tools
blocks.alt: Design tools arranged on a screen
blocks.caption: Setting up tools once saves time on every design after.

blocks.text: Brand Kit: your colours and fonts in one place

Canva's **Brand Kit** (found under Brand on the home screen or in the menu) stores your logo, colours and fonts so they appear at the top of every colour and font menu. The full Brand Kit, with logos, multiple palettes and uploaded fonts, is a Canva Pro feature, and what the free plan includes has changed over time, so check what your account shows. If you are on the free plan and cannot save a kit, use two workarounds:

items: Keep a design called "Brand guide" open in a second tab and copy elements from it.
After you use a colour once in a design, Canva shows it under **Document colours**, so set your colours early in each design and they stay one tap away.

blocks.text: Make a master template

Instead of starting from Canva's templates every time, make your own. Design one post you are proud of, then **duplicate** it (tap the three dots on the design in Projects and choose Make a copy) every time you need a new one. Keep the layout, fonts and colours; only change the words and the photo. This is how big brands keep every post consistent.
Good master templates for a small business include: a product post, a price list, a customer review post, a "we are open" or "new stock" announcement, and a story with a question sticker space.
Resizing for different platforms

Canva Pro has a **Resize** feature (Canva calls the newer version Magic Switch) that copies your design into new sizes in one tap. On the free plan, you can do it by hand: create a new design at the new size, then copy and paste elements across from the original. Either way, always check the result, because text near the edges may be cut off or need moving.
Background remover and folders

The **Background Remover** (under Edit photo, then BG Remover) cuts a product or person out of a photo in one tap. It is a Pro feature in Canva. A free alternative is to photograph products on a plain white or single-colour surface from the start, which looks clean without editing. To stay organised, create **folders** in Projects, such as "Templates", "Weekly posts" and "Print", and move each design into the right one.

Name designs clearly as you save them, for example "Price list master" or "Status new stock June". Canva gives new designs generic names such as "Untitled design", and after a month you will have dozens of them. A clear name plus a folder means you find any design in seconds instead of scrolling.
Sharing a design with a helper

If a family member or staff member helps with your posts, use the **Share** button to invite them by email with edit or view access, or share a template link. They then work on the same design rather than sending screenshots back and forth on WhatsApp, and your brand stays consistent.

blocks.title: The reuse cycle
items: Design one strong master
Duplicate for new post
Change words and photo
Post and note results
Improve the master
blocks.caption: Each round of reuse makes the master template better and faster to use.

blocks.title: Worked example: one design, three sizes
blocks.context: For example, Ruth runs a tailoring shop in Port Harcourt and is announcing a Christmas sewing deadline on Instagram feed, WhatsApp Status and a printed notice for her shop window.
steps: She designs the announcement as an Instagram portrait post at 1080 x 1350 using her master template.
She creates a new Your Story design at 1080 x 1920, copies the heading, date and logo across, and moves the heading lower so it sits away from the profile picture area at the top.
She creates an A4 flyer, pastes the same elements, and enlarges the deadline date so it can be read from the street.
She downloads the two social designs as PNG and the flyer as PDF Print.
She moves all three into a folder named "Christmas 2026".
blocks.result: Three matching pieces are ready in about 25 minutes, all clearly from the same shop, and next year she only changes the dates.

blocks.title: Check every resize
blocks.text: Automatic resizing is a starting point, not a finished design. Always zoom in and look for text cut off at the edges, logos overlapping photos, and words that are now too small.

takeaways: Set your brand colours and fonts once so they are always one tap away.
Duplicate your own master designs instead of starting from scratch.
Know the main sizes: 1080 x 1080, 1080 x 1350 and 1080 x 1920.
Always check a resized design by eye before posting.

activity.title: Build your template set
steps: Save your brand colours and fonts in Brand Kit, or set up a Brand guide design if you are on the free plan.
Create three master templates: a product post, a price list and a story.
Resize one of them into a second size and fix anything that breaks.
Create a Templates folder in Projects and move the masters into it.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of your Templates folder showing three master designs, plus the resized design as a PNG.

quiz.q: Chika's flyer has the event name, date, venue, five sponsor names and a long prayer all in the same size. What should she fix first?
options: Create hierarchy: one big hook, smaller details, move extra text to the caption
Add more colours so it looks lively
Change every line to a script font
quiz.explain: When everything is the same size, nothing stands out. Hierarchy tells the viewer what to read first, and extra text belongs in the caption.

quiz.q: Which text and background pair is most likely to fail on a phone screen in sunlight?
options: Dark navy text on light grey
quiz.explain: Light yellow on white has very low contrast. WCAG asks for at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text, and this pair is far below it.

quiz.q: Ngozi wants to register her bakery logo as a trademark later. How should she build the logo in Canva?
options: From any free Canva template logo
From text and basic shapes only, or have an original logo designed
By downloading a logo from Google Images
quiz.explain: Canva's content licence does not allow trademarking designs built from its stock elements and templates. Text and basic shapes, or original artwork, avoid this problem.

quiz.q: Which file type should Funmi choose for a menu she is sending to a printer?
quiz.explain: PDF Print is designed for printing and keeps text sharp at print quality.

quiz.q: Zainab made a perfect Instagram square post and wants a WhatsApp Status version. What is the correct size and approach?
options: Create a 1080 x 1920 design, move elements across, then check edges and spacing
Stretch the square to fit; nothing else needed
Use 1200 x 628 because it is wider
Post the square; status crops it automatically and perfectly
quiz.explain: Status and stories are 1080 x 1920 (9:16). After resizing or copying, always check that nothing is cut off or crowded.

quiz.q: What does a crown icon on a Canva template element mean?
options: It is the most popular element
It is a Canva Pro element that needs a paid plan
It is free for commercial use without limits
It was made by the Canva founder
quiz.explain: The crown marks Pro content. Free plan users can see it but must pay or swap it for a free element.

modules.title: Graphic Content for Social Media
modules.overview: Design posts, carousels, infographics, professional documents, stories, animated posts and simple ads that are sized correctly, honest, and built to get a real response from customers and partners.

lessons.title: Instagram and Facebook posts that stop the scroll
objectives: Choose the right post format: single image, carousel or story
Design a feed post with a clear hook and call to action
Write a caption that sells without sounding desperate
Plan a carousel that teaches or shows a product in steps

blocks.text: People scroll Instagram and Facebook fast. Your post has about the time of one thumb movement to make someone stop. That means the **first thing they see** (the image and the first line of the caption) must be clear, relevant and easy to read on a small screen. This lesson shows you how to design feed posts, carousels and captions for small businesses and community groups.

blocks.name: social-media-post
blocks.alt: A social media post on a phone
blocks.caption: Your post must be understood in one quick glance while someone scrolls.

blocks.text: Choose the right format

head: Format
Size
Best for
rows: One product, one announcement, one quote or review
Same size on every slide, up to 10 or more slides depending on the platform
Step by step tips, a product range, before and after
Daily updates, behind the scenes, polls, time-limited offers

blocks.text: Portrait posts at 1080 x 1350 take up more of the screen in the feed than squares, so many creators prefer them for product photos. Stories disappear after 24 hours unless you save them as **Highlights** on your profile, which is a good place to keep a permanent price list or "How to order" story.
The anatomy of a strong feed post

items: **One message per post.** A post about your new hair braiding style should not also announce your church programme.
**A hook in large text**, five to eight words: "Knotless braids, ready in 4 hours".
**A real photo** of your product or work, sharp and well lit. Real work builds trust faster than stock photos.
**Your brand colours and logo**, small, in the same corner every time.
**A call to action (CTA)**: what should she do now? "Send DM to book", "Tap the link in bio", "WhatsApp 0803 000 0000".

blocks.text: Carousels that people swipe

A carousel works like a mini lesson or catalogue. Slide 1 is the cover: a strong promise such as "5 ways to keep your wig fresh". Slides 2 to 6 deliver one point each, with large text. The last slide is your CTA and contact. In Canva, design all slides as pages in one design, keep the same layout on every page, and download all pages as PNG. Then select them together when you post. Design a small arrow or the words "Swipe" on slide 1 so people know there is more.

blocks.title: Carousel structure
items: Cover with promise
One point per slide
Proof or example
Call to action slide
blocks.caption: A carousel works best when it moves in a clear line from promise to action.

blocks.text: Captions that do the selling

Only the first line or two of a caption shows before "more", so put the most important words first. A simple caption formula is **Hook, Value, Proof, Action**. Use short lines and two or three relevant emojis at most. Add a few specific hashtags that real customers might search, such as your city and service (#AbujaCaterer, #LagosMakeupArtist), rather than thirty general ones.

blocks.title: Worked example: a product post and caption for a shea butter seller
blocks.context: For example, Hauwa makes whipped shea butter in Kaduna and sells 250 g jars for about 3,500 naira (approximate). She wants more orders from Instagram.
steps: Photo: she shoots a jar near a window in daylight, lid off, on a plain wooden tray, with a few raw shea nuts beside it.
Design: a 1080 x 1350 Canva post using her master template; hook text "Whipped shea butter, 100% from Kaduna" at the top; small logo bottom right.
Caption line 1 (hook): "Dry skin this harmattan? This is for you."
Caption body: three short lines on what is in it (only shea butter and coconut oil), the size (250 g), and the price (3,500 naira).
Proof: "Over 40 jars sent out this month" (she counts her own orders, so it is true).
Action: "WhatsApp 0806 000 0000 to order. Delivery within Kaduna."
blocks.result: The post has one clear message, a real photo, and a caption that answers price, size and how to order, which are the three questions customers ask most.

blocks.text: Facebook differences

Facebook uses the same square and portrait sizes, and posts made for Instagram usually work there too. Facebook audiences in Nigeria often include older customers and community groups, so posts with clear prices, location and phone numbers do well. Facebook also lets you post into **groups** you belong to, such as a local buy and sell group; read each group's rules first, because many allow selling posts only on certain days.
After you post

Reply to comments and messages quickly, ideally within a few hours, because a fast reply often decides whether a customer buys from you or the next seller. On a professional or creator account, open **Insights** on each post after a few days. Note which posts got the most saves, shares and messages, not only likes. Saves and messages show real interest, and those are the post types to make more of.

blocks.title: Only post true claims
blocks.text: Never claim a product cures a disease or is "NAFDAC approved" unless it has a real NAFDAC registration number. False claims can lead to complaints, account reports and legal trouble.

takeaways: One message per post, with a clear hook and call to action.
Use 1080 x 1350 for product posts and 1080 x 1920 for stories.
Carousels: cover promise, one point per slide, CTA at the end.
Captions: hook, value, proof, action, with the important words first.

activity.title: Design a carousel for your business
steps: Choose a topic: five tips, a product range, or how to order.
In Canva, make a 1080 x 1350 design with five pages using your master template.
Write a cover promise, three content slides and a CTA slide.
Write a caption using Hook, Value, Proof, Action.
Download all pages as PNG.
activity.evidence: The five PNG slides and your caption saved as a note on your phone.

lessons.title: Infographics and simple charts that tell the truth
objectives: Decide when an infographic is better than plain text
Choose the right chart type for your numbers
Build a simple infographic and chart in Canva
Avoid charts that mislead people

blocks.text: An **infographic** is a graphic that explains information quickly using a mix of short text, icons, numbers and simple charts. Infographics are excellent for steps ("How to register for our training"), comparisons ("Ankara vs Lace: care tips"), timelines ("Our programme in 6 weeks") and results ("What our cooperative did this year"). They are shared widely on WhatsApp because one image carries the whole message.

blocks.name: visual-data
blocks.alt: A person reading charts on a screen
blocks.caption: A good infographic turns numbers and steps into something understood at a glance.

blocks.text: Plan before you design

items: Write your one main message in a single sentence, such as "Our savings group grew from 12 to 30 members in one year".
List the three to six facts that support it. Use only numbers you can check, such as your own records.
Decide the shape of the information: steps, comparison, timeline, or numbers over time.
Only then open Canva and search templates for "infographic" or "timeline".

blocks.text: Choose the right chart

head: Your data
Best chart
Example
rows: Compare amounts across a few groups
Sales of four products this month
Monthly savings from January to June
Pie or donut chart, maximum 4 to 5 slices
How a 10,000 naira contribution is spent

blocks.text: Building a chart in Canva

In the Canva editor, tap **+**, then search Elements for **Charts**. Choose a bar, line or pie chart and tap it to add. Tap the chart, then **Edit** (or Data) to type your labels and values into the small table. Canva redraws the chart as you type. Change the chart colours to your brand palette, and make the labels large enough to read on a phone. Delete any decoration that does not help understanding.
Honest charts

Charts can mislead, even by accident. The three most common problems are: a bar chart whose axis does not start at zero, which makes small differences look huge; a pie chart with too many slices, which nobody can read; and missing labels or units, so people do not know if a number is naira, people or percentages. Always label units, start bar charts at zero, and write the source and date of your numbers in small text at the bottom, for example "Source: group records, Jan to Dec 2025".
Layout tips for infographics on a phone

items: Use a portrait size (1080 x 1350) so the infographic fills the screen.
Read from top to bottom: title, then sections in order, then source.
Give each section an icon from Canva Elements, and use the same icon style (all line icons, or all filled icons) throughout.
Keep text to short phrases. If a section needs a paragraph, it belongs in the caption.
Use numbers in big type and words in smaller type, so the eye goes to the figures first.

blocks.text: Test it the WhatsApp way: send the image to yourself, open it on your phone without zooming, and check if every word can be read. WhatsApp compresses images, so tiny text that looked fine in Canva can become blurry once shared.

blocks.title: Honest chart checklist
items: Bars start at zero
Units clearly labelled
Five slices or fewer
Source and date shown
One clear takeaway title
blocks.caption: Run through these five checks before you share any chart.

blocks.title: Worked example: a yearly report graphic for a savings group
blocks.context: For example, Grace is secretary of a women's thrift (ajo) group in Akure and wants a single image for the end-of-year meeting and the WhatsApp group.
steps: Main message: "Together we saved more than ever in 2025."
Facts from the group's record book: members grew from 12 to 30; total savings by quarter were 360,000, 540,000, 810,000 and 900,000 naira (illustrative figures for this example).
She chooses a 1080 x 1350 Canva design: a title at the top, two big-number blocks ("30 members" and "2,610,000 naira saved"), then a bar chart of the four quarters.
She sets the bars in the group's green, labels the axis "Naira saved", and adds "Source: group records, 2025" at the bottom.
blocks.result: Members understand the year's progress in seconds, and the total is correct because she added it up herself before designing.

blocks.text: Timelines and process graphics

Not every infographic needs numbers. A **process graphic** shows steps in order with arrows or numbered circles, such as "How to join our cooperative: 1. Fill the form, 2. Pay the 2,000 naira registration (approximate), 3. Attend orientation, 4. Start monthly savings". A **timeline** shows events along a line, such as a six-week training programme. In Canva, search Elements for "timeline" or "process arrows" and replace the text with your own steps.

blocks.title: Accessibility
blocks.text: Do not rely on colour alone to show differences: some people are colour blind. Add labels or numbers directly on bars and slices.

takeaways: Plan the message and facts before you open Canva.
Bar for comparisons, line for change over time, pie only for a few parts of a whole.
Canva's Charts element lets you type data and restyle it in brand colours.
Start bars at zero, label units, and show the source and date.

activity.title: Make a one-page infographic
steps: Choose a real topic you have numbers or steps for (sales, savings, a process).
Write the one-sentence message and three to six facts.
Build it in Canva with one chart or one timeline and your brand colours.
Run the honest chart checklist.
Download as PNG.
activity.evidence: Your infographic PNG plus a photo of the notes or records where the numbers came from.

lessons.title: LinkedIn and professional graphics: banners, CVs and certificates
objectives: Design a LinkedIn banner and choose a professional profile photo
Create a clean one-page CV or company profile in Canva
Make a certificate or programme cover for an event
Adjust tone, colours and layout for professional audiences

blocks.text: Professional audiences, such as employers, NGOs, banks, sponsors and corporate clients, judge you quickly on how clean your materials look. **LinkedIn** is the main professional social network, and many recruiters and partners in Nigeria check it before replying to an email. Canva has templates for LinkedIn banners, CVs (resumes), company profiles, letterheads and certificates. The design rules from Module 1 still apply, but with a calmer style: more white space, fewer colours, and no stickers or decorative fonts.

blocks.name: online-profile
blocks.alt: A professional online profile on a screen
blocks.caption: Your profile and documents are often the first impression a partner or employer gets.

blocks.text: Your LinkedIn profile visuals

items: **Profile photo**: head and shoulders, your face filling about 60% of the frame, plain background, daylight from a window in front of you, and a friendly expression. Upload at least 400 x 400 pixels.

**Banner (background photo)**: 1584 x 396 pixels. Search Canva for "LinkedIn background". Include your name or business name and one line on what you do. Keep text towards the right and centre, because your profile photo covers the lower left on many screens.
**Featured posts**: share your best Canva graphics or a PDF portfolio in the Featured section.

blocks.text: A one-page CV that reads well

Canva's resume templates look attractive, but some are hard for computer systems (applicant tracking systems) to read. Choose a simple, single column template with real text, not text inside images, and download as **PDF Standard**. A clear CV order is: name and contacts, a two-line profile, experience (most recent first, with results), education, skills, and referees on request. Use one font family, 10 to 12 point body text when printed on A4, and plenty of space between sections.
Company profile and certificates

A **company profile** is a short document (often 4 to 8 pages) that introduces your business to partners: who you are, services, past work with photos, testimonials and contact details. In Canva, create it as a multi-page A4 document. Put your CAC registration number on the contact page only if your business is actually registered.

**Certificates** for training or volunteering are a common Canva task in community groups. Use A4 landscape, a calm border, the organisation's logo, the recipient's name as the biggest text, the reason for the award, the date, and signature lines. If you need many certificates with different names, Canva has a **Bulk Create** feature (a Pro feature) that fills names from a list; on the free plan, duplicate the page and change the name on each copy.
Letterheads and email signatures

Two more professional pieces worth making once: a **letterhead** (A4 page with your logo and contact details at the top or bottom, used for letters and quotations) and an **email signature** image. Canva has templates for both. Keep the email signature small and simple: name, role, business name, phone number and website. A signature image that is too large is often blocked or shown as an attachment by email apps, so plain text is often the safer choice, with the logo only if it displays properly.
When sending professional documents, name files clearly, for example "Esther_Okafor_CV_2026.pdf" rather than "Untitled design (3).pdf". Small details like this signal care.

blocks.title: Social style vs professional style
items: Social media post
Professional document
blocks.caption: Professional materials use more space and fewer colours to signal trust.

blocks.title: Worked example: a LinkedIn banner for a bookkeeper
blocks.context: For example, Esther is a freelance bookkeeper in Abuja who serves small shops and wants her LinkedIn profile to look trustworthy.
steps: She opens Canva, creates a custom design of 1584 x 396 pixels, and chooses a simple template with a navy background.
She types her line: "Bookkeeping for small businesses in Abuja. Clear records, monthly reports." in white, 40 to 48 points, placed to the right of centre.
She adds her website or email in smaller text below and leaves the lower left corner empty for the profile photo.
She takes a new profile photo by a window at 10am, with a plain wall behind, using the 2x zoom on her phone to avoid distortion of her face.
She uploads both and checks the profile on her phone and on a laptop.
blocks.result: The banner and photo now say clearly who she is and who she serves, and nothing important is hidden behind the profile photo.

blocks.title: Check how it prints
blocks.text: Before printing many certificates or profiles, print one copy. Colours often look darker on paper than on a bright phone screen, and thin borders near the edge may be cut off by the printer. Keep important items at least 5 mm inside the page edge.

blocks.title: Be accurate on documents
blocks.text: Only list qualifications, registrations and clients that are real. A polished design with false details can end a professional relationship quickly.

takeaways: Professional design means more white space, fewer colours, no stickers.
LinkedIn banner: 1584 x 396 pixels, keep text away from the profile photo area.
Use a simple single column CV and download as PDF.
Certificates: recipient's name is the biggest text; duplicate pages or use Bulk Create for many names.

activity.title: Refresh your professional look
steps: Take a new head and shoulders profile photo in daylight.
Design a LinkedIn banner at 1584 x 396 with your name or business and one line on what you do.
Design a one-page CV or a one-page business profile in Canva.
Download the CV or profile as PDF and check it on your phone.
activity.evidence: Your banner PNG, profile photo and PDF document saved in your course album.

lessons.title: Ads, stories and simple animated posts
objectives: Design a story with safe zones for text and stickers
Create a simple animated post in Canva and export it as MP4
Prepare a basic ad design that follows platform guidelines
Write ad text with one clear offer and one action

blocks.text: Stories, short animated posts and paid ads are where much of the attention is on Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp today. They are all vertical or square, short, and must work with or without sound. Canva can make all three on your phone.

blocks.name: mobile-marketing
blocks.alt: A person promoting a product on a mobile phone
blocks.caption: Stories and ads are designed for vertical phone screens first.

blocks.text: Designing stories: mind the safe zone

Stories are 1080 x 1920 pixels. The top of the screen shows your profile name and a progress bar, and the bottom shows the reply box. If you place text there, it gets covered. Keep important text and faces inside the middle area, leaving roughly **250 pixels clear at the top and bottom**. In Canva you can add a rectangle of that height as a guide while designing, then delete it before downloading.

items: Use one idea per story frame; people tap through in a second or two.
Leave space for interactive stickers you add in the app later, such as polls, questions or links.
For WhatsApp Status, the same 9:16 size works well.

blocks.text: Simple animation in Canva

Movement catches the eye. In Canva, select a text or element and tap **Animate** to choose an effect such as Rise, Pan, Fade or Typewriter. Tap on an empty part of the page and choose a **Page animation** to animate everything at once. Set the page duration (for example 5 seconds) with the timing button. Download as **MP4 Video** for movement, or GIF for a short loop without sound. Keep animation gentle: one or two moving items is enough, and text must stay on screen long enough to read.
Paid ads: the basics

On Facebook and Instagram, ads are created in **Meta Ads Manager** or by tapping "Boost post" on a professional account. You choose a goal (such as messages on WhatsApp), an audience (location, age range, interests), a daily budget and how many days. Meta's own guidance recommends that ad images use little text, and ads must follow Meta's Advertising Standards: no false claims, no before and after images for weight loss, and careful rules on health and financial products. Read the standards before boosting anything health or money related.

head: Ad element
Good practice
rows: Hook, benefit, price or offer, how to order
Choose one action, such as Send WhatsApp message
Start small and run a short test before spending more

blocks.text: Writing ad text that works

Strong ad text has one offer and one action. Start with who it is for and what problem it solves, give the price or the offer, and end with the single action you want. Avoid ALL CAPITALS and many exclamation marks, which look like spam. Write as you would speak to a customer in your shop. For example: "Charger keeps dying? Original 20W fast chargers, tested before you pay. From 6,500 naira. Tap Send message to order."

Keep records of each ad: the date, the design used, the money spent and the number of real enquiries and sales. Divide the money spent by the number of sales to know your cost per sale. If an ad costs more per sale than your profit on the item, stop it and change the design, the offer or the audience.

blocks.title: A short ad test
items: Day 1: design two versions
Days 2 to 4: run both
Day 5: compare messages
Day 6: keep the winner
blocks.caption: Testing two small versions before spending more shows which design actually brings messages.

blocks.title: Worked example: an animated story and a small ad test for a phone accessories shop
blocks.context: For example, Kemi sells phone cases and chargers in Computer Village, Ikeja, and wants more WhatsApp orders.
steps: She designs a 1080 x 1920 story: product photo in the middle, hook "Fast chargers, 1 week warranty" with a Rise animation, price "from 6,500 naira (approximate)" and "Send us a message" placed above the bottom 250 pixels.
She sets the page to 6 seconds and downloads as MP4.
She makes a second version with a different hook: "Original chargers, tested in front of you".
She boosts each version with the goal of WhatsApp messages, for 3 days, at the same small daily budget, to people around Lagos.
On day 5 she counts real WhatsApp chats from each version: version A 9 chats, version B 21 chats (her own illustrative count).
blocks.result: She stops version A and keeps version B, because the evidence shows customers care more about the product being genuine than about speed.

blocks.title: Ad scams target sellers too
blocks.text: Meta will never ask for your password or payment over WhatsApp or a random message. Ignore messages claiming your page will be deleted unless you click a link. Manage ads only inside the official Facebook, Instagram or Meta Business Suite apps.

takeaways: Stories are 1080 x 1920; keep text out of the top and bottom 250 pixels.
Use Canva's Animate tool gently and download as MP4.
Ads must follow Meta's Advertising Standards; avoid false or risky claims.
Test two small versions and keep the one that brings real results.

activity.title: Make an animated story and an ad plan
steps: Design a 1080 x 1920 story with a product, a hook, a price and a CTA inside the safe zone.
Animate one or two elements and download it as MP4.
Create a second version with a different hook.
Write a short ad plan: goal, audience location, small daily budget, number of days, and how you will count results.
activity.evidence: Both MP4 stories plus your written ad plan as a phone note or screenshot.

quiz.q: Tolu's story text keeps getting hidden behind her profile name and the reply box. What should she do?
options: Keep text inside the middle area, about 250 pixels clear at top and bottom
quiz.explain: The top and bottom of a 1080 x 1920 story are covered by app controls, so important text belongs in the middle safe zone.

quiz.q: Which chart best shows how a cooperative's savings changed from January to June?
quiz.explain: Line charts show change over time clearly.

quiz.q: Amina's bar chart axis starts at 90,000 naira, so a 5% difference looks huge. What is the problem?
options: She should use a pie chart with ten slices
The bars should start at zero so the comparison is honest
quiz.explain: Bar charts that do not start at zero exaggerate differences and mislead viewers.

quiz.q: What is the recommended LinkedIn banner size?
quiz.explain: LinkedIn background photos are 1584 x 396 pixels.

quiz.q: Which caption opening is strongest for a shea butter post?
options: "Good morning everyone, hope you are all fine, God bless"
"Dry skin this harmattan? This is for you."
quiz.explain: Only the first line shows before "more". A hook that names the customer's problem makes people stop and read.

quiz.q: Kemi tested two ad versions. Version A brought 9 WhatsApp chats and version B brought 21 with the same budget and days. What should she do next?
options: Double the budget on version A
Keep version B and stop version A
Change the audience on both at once
quiz.explain: With the same budget and time, version B performed better, so she keeps the winner and stops the weaker one.

modules.title: Video and Audio with Phone Tools
modules.overview: Use your phone camera with good light and steady shots, edit clean short videos in CapCut, plan Reels and Shorts that people watch to the end, and record clear voice audio for voiceovers and simple podcasts.

lessons.title: Your phone camera for video: settings, light and steady shots
objectives: Set your phone camera's resolution, frame rate and gridlines for social video
Use tap to focus and exposure lock so footage does not flicker
Hold or mount the phone for steady shots
Plan a simple shot list of wide, medium and close-up shots

blocks.text: You do not need an expensive camera to make good video. Modern smartphones record sharp video. What makes most phone video look poor is not the phone but **shaky hands, bad light, a dirty lens and messy sound**. Fix those four and your video will look far more professional. This lesson covers the camera side; sound is covered in Lesson 3.4.

blocks.name: movie-camera
blocks.caption: Your phone is a capable video camera once you control light and steadiness.

blocks.text: Before you press record

items: **Clean the lens** with a soft cloth. A greasy fingerprint makes everything look hazy, and it is the most common cause of soft, foggy footage.
**Check storage and battery.** One minute of 1080p video can take roughly 100 MB or more depending on the phone, and 4K takes much more. Clear space first.
**Turn on gridlines** in camera settings. They divide the screen into nine boxes and help you keep the horizon level and place your subject.

**Choose resolution and frame rate.** For social media, **1080p at 30 frames per second (fps)** is a sensible default: sharp enough, smaller files, less data to upload. Use 4K only if you have storage and a reason.
**Switch on airplane mode or Do Not Disturb** so a call does not interrupt a good take.

blocks.text: Vertical or horizontal?

Shoot **vertical (9:16)** for Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Stories and WhatsApp Status. Shoot **horizontal (16:9)** for standard YouTube videos and anything shown on a TV or projector. Decide before you start, because cropping later loses quality and can cut off people's heads.
Focus and exposure

Phones adjust focus and brightness automatically, which can cause the picture to pulse lighter and darker as you move. Tap on your subject's face to focus. On iPhone, press and hold to lock focus and exposure (AE/AF Lock appears). On most Android phones, tap the subject and a lock or a sun slider appears. Slide the sun icon down slightly if bright areas, such as a white wall or the sky, are losing detail.
Light: the biggest free upgrade

items: Face a window with daylight falling on your face. Do not stand with the window behind you, or you become a dark shape.
Avoid harsh midday sun directly overhead, which makes dark shadows under the eyes. Shade or early morning and late afternoon light is softer.
Turn off mixed lights: a yellow bulb plus blue daylight gives strange skin colours.
A cheap ring light helps at night, but place it in front of you at eye level, slightly above.

blocks.text: Steady shots

Shaky video is tiring to watch. Hold the phone with both hands and tuck your elbows against your body. Walk slowly with bent knees if you must move. Better still, use a phone tripod or rest the phone against books on a table. Many phones also have video stabilisation; leave it on. Use the main (1x) lens for the best quality; digital zoom beyond the phone's optical lenses makes the picture soft. If you need to be closer, walk closer.

blocks.title: Three-shot sequence
items: Wide: show the place
Medium: show the action
Close-up: show the detail
blocks.caption: Cutting between wide, medium and close shots makes even a simple video feel professional.

blocks.text: Plan a shot list

A **shot list** is a short plan of each clip you need. Professional editors cut between different shot sizes to keep video interesting. A **wide shot** shows the whole scene, a **medium shot** shows a person from the waist up or hands working, and a **close-up** shows a detail, such as a stitch or a sauce bubbling. Record each clip for at least 5 to 10 seconds so you have room to trim.

blocks.title: Worked example: shooting a 30-second video of making zobo
blocks.context: For example, Nkechi sells zobo drinks in Owerri and wants a vertical video for Instagram Reels and WhatsApp Status.
steps: Setup: she cleans the lens, sets 1080p 30fps, turns on gridlines and airplane mode, and places the phone on a small tripod by her kitchen window at 9am.
Shot 1 (wide, 8 seconds): her clean kitchen counter with ingredients laid out.
Shot 2 (close-up, 6 seconds): dried hibiscus leaves poured into a pot.
Shot 3 (medium, 8 seconds): her hands adding ginger and pineapple peel, face not needed.
Shot 4 (close-up, 6 seconds): chilled zobo poured into a branded bottle, condensation visible.
Shot 5 (medium, 6 seconds): she holds the bottle, smiles and says "Order on WhatsApp".
blocks.result: She has five clips totalling 34 seconds of usable footage, all steady and bright, ready to edit into a 25 to 30 second Reel in CapCut.

blocks.title: Safe filming at work
blocks.text: When filming cooking, keep the phone and tripod away from hot pots and gas flames, and never film while driving or crossing a road. If you film customers or children, ask permission first.

takeaways: Clean lens, steady phone and good light matter more than an expensive phone.
1080p at 30fps is a sensible default for social video.
Shoot vertical for Reels, Shorts, Status and Stories; horizontal for YouTube and screens.
Plan wide, medium and close-up shots, each 5 to 10 seconds long.

activity.title: Record a three-shot sequence
steps: Clean your lens and set 1080p 30fps with gridlines on.
Choose a simple process from your work or home.
Record one wide, one medium and one close-up shot, each 5 to 10 seconds, by window light.
Lock focus on your subject for at least one shot.
Watch the clips and note one thing to improve.
activity.evidence: The three video clips in your course album and a short note on what you would improve.

lessons.title: CapCut basics: trim, arrange, caption and export
objectives: Start a CapCut project and import clips in order
Split, trim, reorder and delete clips on the timeline
Add text, auto captions, music and transitions
Export a video at the right resolution for social media

blocks.text: **CapCut** is a free video editing app for Android, iPhone and computers, made by ByteDance, the company behind TikTok. It is popular because it does a lot on a phone: cutting clips, captions, music, effects and exporting without a watermark. Some features and effects are marked Pro and need a paid plan; the core editing tools in this lesson are available for free at the time of writing, but check your own app, because plans change.

blocks.name: video-files
blocks.caption: Editing turns separate clips into one clear story.

blocks.text: The CapCut screen

head: Area
What it does
rows: Plays your video so you can check it
Your clips in a row; the white vertical line is the playhead, showing the current moment
Edit, Audio, Text, Effects, Overlay, Captions, Format and more
Choose resolution and frame rate, then save the finished video

blocks.text: Step by step: your first edit

items: Open CapCut and tap **New project**. Select your clips in the order you want them, then tap **Add**.
**Set the format**: tap Format (or Ratio) and choose 9:16 for Reels, Shorts and Status.
**Trim**: tap a clip on the timeline. Drag the white handles at either end to cut the slow start and the end.
**Split**: move the playhead to where you want to cut, select the clip and tap **Split**. Then select the unwanted part and tap **Delete**.
**Reorder**: press and hold a clip, then drag it to a new position.
**Text**: tap Text, then Add text, type a short title, and choose a clear font and your brand colour. Drag the text box ends on the timeline to set how long it stays.
**Auto captions**: tap Captions (or Text, then Auto captions), choose the spoken language, and CapCut writes captions from your voice. Read them carefully and fix wrong words.
**Music**: tap Audio, then Sounds, and choose a track from CapCut's library. Lower its volume so speech stays clear.
**Transitions**: tap the small white square between two clips and choose a simple cut or fade. Use the same transition throughout.

blocks.text: Edit for attention

items: Show the most interesting moment in the **first 2 to 3 seconds**: the finished product, the result, or a question.
Keep each clip short, usually 1 to 4 seconds in a fast social video.
Cut silences and "ehm" pauses.
Many people watch without sound, so captions and on-screen text carry the message.

blocks.text: Export settings

Tap the resolution label beside Export. For social media, choose **1080p** and **30fps**. Higher settings make much bigger files that cost more data to upload and are often compressed by the platform anyway. CapCut may add an ending clip with its logo at the end of the timeline; you can tap it and delete it before exporting. Save to your phone, then upload from your gallery or share directly.
Saving your work and data

CapCut saves projects on your phone as you work, so you can close the app and continue later from the projects list on the home screen. Projects use storage, so delete old drafts you no longer need. Editing itself works offline once the clips are on your phone, but the music library, templates and auto captions need internet, so do those steps when you are on Wi-Fi or have data. After exporting, watch the whole video once on your phone with sound and once without sound before you post it.

blocks.title: CapCut edit order
items: Import and set 9:16
Trim and arrange clips
Add text and captions
Add music, check volume
Export 1080p 30fps
blocks.caption: Working in this order prevents redoing captions after moving clips.

blocks.title: Worked example: editing the zobo Reel
blocks.context: For example, Nkechi from Lesson 3.1 has five clips totalling 34 seconds and wants a 25-second Reel.
steps: She creates a new project, adds the five clips in order and sets the format to 9:16.
She moves clip 4 (pouring chilled zobo) to the start as a 2-second hook, then trims each other clip to 3 to 6 seconds.
Timing check: 2 + 5 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 4 = 25 seconds (she split the pouring clip so it appears at the start and again near the end).
She adds text "Fresh zobo, made today" in her brand red for the first 3 seconds, and "500 naira per bottle (approximate), Owerri delivery" near the end.
She uses auto captions for her spoken line and corrects "so bow" to "zobo".
She adds a calm Afrobeat track from CapCut's library at 20% volume and exports at 1080p 30fps.
blocks.result: A 25-second vertical Reel with a strong opening, readable text, correct captions and music that does not drown her voice.

blocks.title: Music and copyright
blocks.text: Songs from CapCut's library are licensed for use inside the app's terms, but a popular song added from your own phone may be muted or blocked on Instagram, Facebook or YouTube. For business ads, use music clearly licensed for commercial use, such as the YouTube Audio Library or Meta Sound Collection.

takeaways: Set the format to 9:16 before editing vertical videos.
Trim, split and reorder to remove slow parts and start with the best moment.
Always proofread auto captions.
Export at 1080p 30fps and delete any added ending clip if you do not want it.

activity.title: Edit a 20 to 30 second video
steps: Use the three or more clips you recorded in Lesson 3.1.
Start a CapCut project in 9:16 and arrange the clips with the best moment first.
Trim to 20 to 30 seconds total.
Add one title, captions or on-screen text, and quiet music.
Export at 1080p 30fps.
activity.evidence: The exported video file and a screenshot of your CapCut timeline.

lessons.title: Reels, Shorts and TikTok: planning short videos that get watched
objectives: Explain how Reels, YouTube Shorts and TikTok differ in length and use
Write a short video script with a hook, value and call to action
Choose a repeatable short video format for your business
Read basic insights such as views, watch time and shares

blocks.text: Short vertical videos (Instagram Reels, Facebook Reels, YouTube Shorts and TikTok) are how many new customers discover small businesses. The platforms show them to people who do not follow you yet, if the video keeps people watching. Your job is to make a short video that answers one question or shows one result, very clearly.

blocks.name: video-influencer
blocks.alt: A woman recording a short video with her phone
blocks.caption: Short videos reach new people when they keep viewers watching to the end.

blocks.text: The platforms at a glance

head: Platform
Shape
Typical length that works for beginners
Good to know
rows: Shared to Facebook too if you link accounts
Under 60 seconds is a safe target
Can lead viewers to your longer YouTube videos
Short clips; long videos are split into parts

blocks.text: Maximum lengths on these platforms change often, so check the app. For a beginner, shorter is safer: a tight 20 to 30 second video that people finish usually does better than a long one they abandon.
Script structure: Hook, Value, Action

items: **Hook (0 to 3 seconds)**: a strong first image and line. "Stop wasting your tomatoes", "This is how we pack 100 orders a day", or show the finished result first.
**Value (middle)**: the tip, the steps, the transformation or the story. One idea only.
**Action (last 3 to 5 seconds)**: what to do now. Follow for more, send a message, visit the shop.

blocks.text: Write the script in short spoken lines, as you would talk to a friend. Read it aloud and time it. About 2 to 3 spoken words per second is a natural pace, so a 30-second video holds roughly 60 to 80 words of speech.
Repeatable formats
Instead of inventing something new every day, choose two or three formats you can repeat. Repeating formats makes production faster and helps your audience know what to expect.

items: **Process video**: show how you make or prepare something (sewing a dress, baking, packing an order).
**Before and after**: a hairstyle, a cleaned shoe, a decorated hall. (Do not use before and after for weight loss or skin treatment claims.)
**Quick tip**: one useful tip linked to your product (how to store shea butter in hot weather).
**Customer question answered**: read a real question and answer it in 20 seconds.
**Day in the life**: short clips of your work day, showing the human behind the business.

blocks.text: Covers, captions and posting

Choose a clear **cover image** when you post: a frame that shows the product or result with a short title, because the cover appears on your profile grid. Write a caption that repeats the main point in words for people who do not play sound. Post when your customers are usually on their phones; your insights show the hours your followers are most active.

blocks.title: Choosing a short video format
items: Quick tip
Process video
Customer answer
Day in the life
blocks.caption: Pick formats in the top row when you have little time; the right column builds most trust.

blocks.text: Reading the results

On a professional or creator account, open each video's insights after two or three days. Look at **views**, **average watch time** (how long people stayed), **shares** and **saves**, and messages that came from it. If people leave in the first 3 seconds, improve the hook. If they watch but do not act, improve the call to action. Compare formats over several weeks rather than judging one video.

blocks.title: Worked example: a 30-second tip video for a hair stylist
blocks.context: For example, Joy is a hair stylist in Benin City who wants more bookings for braids.
steps: Hook (0 to 3 s): close-up of finished knotless braids, text "Make your braids last 6 weeks".

Value (3 to 24 s): three tips, each on screen for about 7 seconds: wrap with a satin scarf at night; wash scalp gently with diluted shampoo every 2 weeks; do not leave them in longer than about 6 to 8 weeks to protect your edges.
Action (24 to 30 s): Joy on camera, "Book your braids, send a DM", with her location text.
Script length: about 70 spoken words, which fits 30 seconds at a natural pace.
She films in 25 minutes and edits in CapCut in 20 minutes.
blocks.result: A useful, on-brand Reel. After two weeks she checks insights and sees this tip format earns more saves than her plain photo posts, so she makes a tip video every Wednesday.

blocks.title: Trends with care
blocks.text: Trending sounds and challenges can bring views, but only join trends that fit your brand and do not use music you are not allowed to use for business. A clear useful video beats a trend that has nothing to do with what you sell.

takeaways: Short videos reach new people when viewers watch to the end.
Script every video: hook in 3 seconds, one idea, clear action.
About 2 to 3 spoken words per second: 60 to 80 words for 30 seconds.
Repeat two or three formats and judge them on watch time, saves, shares and messages.

activity.title: Script and film a short video
steps: Choose one of the repeatable formats for your business.
Write a Hook, Value, Action script of 60 to 80 words.
Read it aloud and time it.
Film and edit it in CapCut to under 35 seconds.
Post it and note views and watch time after 3 days.
activity.evidence: Your written script, the finished video and a screenshot of its insights after 3 days.

lessons.title: Clear voice and audio: voice notes, voiceovers and simple podcasts
objectives: Record clear voice audio on a phone in an ordinary room
Reduce echo and background noise with simple, cheap fixes
Add a voiceover to a video in CapCut
Plan a short audio series or podcast episode

blocks.text: Viewers forgive slightly soft video, but they leave quickly when the sound is bad. Clear voice is also a powerful content form by itself: WhatsApp voice notes to customers, voiceovers on product videos, audio lessons for your group, and podcasts. Audio is also data friendly, because an audio file is much smaller than a video of the same length.

blocks.name: studio-microphone
blocks.caption: Clear sound keeps people listening, even when the picture is simple.

blocks.text: Where to record

The room matters more than the microphone. Hard bare walls and tiled floors bounce sound and create **echo**. Soft things absorb it. A bedroom with a bed, curtains and a wardrobe of clothes is usually better than an empty sitting room. Some creators record sitting inside or in front of an open wardrobe full of clothes. Turn off fans and air conditioners while recording, close windows facing the road, and record at quieter times of day, avoiding generator noise where you can.
How to hold and use the phone

items: Use the phone's built-in voice recorder app (Voice Recorder on Android, Voice Memos on iPhone), or record directly in CapCut for voiceovers.
Find your phone's microphone, usually a small hole at the bottom edge, and speak towards it.
Keep the phone about a hand's length away, roughly 15 to 20 cm. Too close makes popping sounds on P and B; too far picks up the room.
Speak slightly to the side of the microphone rather than straight into it to reduce breath pops.
Record a 10-second test and listen with earphones before the real recording.

blocks.text: Cheap upgrades

head: Option
Why it helps
Notes
rows: Mic sits close to your mouth, less room noise
Many phones need an adapter if there is no headphone jack
Very clear voice for talking-to-camera videos
Wired and wireless types sold in phone accessory markets
Blankets, curtains, a wardrobe of clothes

blocks.text: Adding a voiceover in CapCut

items: Edit your video first so the timing of clips is final.
Move the playhead to the start, tap **Audio**, then **Record** (the microphone icon).
Hold the record button and speak while watching the preview, or record in short sections.
Tap the recorded audio to adjust volume, and use **Noise reduction** if your version offers it.
Lower background music to around 10 to 20% so your voice stays clear.

blocks.text: A simple podcast or audio series

A **podcast** is a series of audio episodes people can listen to on apps such as Spotify, Apple Podcasts or YouTube. For a community group, a simple audio series can also be shared as files in a WhatsApp or Telegram group. Keep early episodes short, 5 to 15 minutes, on one topic each. Plan an episode with: a short welcome and topic (30 seconds), three main points with examples, a summary, and what is coming next time. Spotify provides a free tool for creators to upload and distribute podcasts; check the current name and terms on Spotify's website, as these have changed over time.
Voice notes to customers

Many Nigerian businesses close sales on WhatsApp voice notes. Keep them short, under one minute, and say the key details clearly: price, size, delivery time and payment method. Then send the same details as a short text message too, so the customer can find them later without replaying the audio. Speak warmly, and never send a voice note from a noisy market if a short text would be clearer.

blocks.title: Audio episode workflow
items: Plan three points
Record in quiet room
Edit out mistakes
Publish and share
Listen to feedback
blocks.caption: Each episode feeds lessons into the next one.

blocks.title: Worked example: a weekly 5-minute audio tip for a farmers' group
blocks.context: For example, Blessing coordinates a women's vegetable farming group in Jos with members who prefer listening to reading.
steps: She plans episode 1: "Three ways to keep tomatoes fresh longer after harvest", with three points and one local example each.
She records in her bedroom at 6am, before the generators start, with the curtains closed and the phone 15 cm away, using wired earphones with a mic.
She records a 10-second test, hears a fan humming, switches it off and starts again.
She trims the start and end in CapCut, exports audio, and the 5-minute file is about 5 MB, far smaller than a video.
She shares it in the group's WhatsApp with a one-line summary and asks members to reply with a voice note question for next week.
blocks.result: Members who rarely read long messages listen and reply, and next week's episode answers their real questions.

blocks.title: Respect privacy
blocks.text: Ask permission before you record or share someone else's voice, such as a customer interview or a voice note question. Remove names or personal details if they ask.

takeaways: The room matters more than the microphone: soft rooms, no fans, quiet times.
Keep the phone about 15 to 20 cm from your mouth and test before recording.
Add voiceovers in CapCut after the edit is final and keep music low.
Start a podcast with short, single-topic episodes of 5 to 15 minutes.

activity.title: Record a 2-minute audio tip
steps: Pick one useful tip related to your work or group.
Prepare a quiet, soft room and switch off fans.
Record a 10-second test, listen with earphones and adjust.
Record a 2-minute tip with a welcome, three points and a closing line.
Trim the start and end and share it to yourself on WhatsApp to check quality.
activity.evidence: The audio file and your short episode plan written as a phone note.

quiz.q: Ada's kitchen video looks hazy and soft even in good light. What should she check first?
quiz.explain: A greasy lens is the most common cause of hazy phone footage, and cleaning it is free.

quiz.q: Which settings are a sensible default for social media video on most phones?
quiz.explain: 1080p at 30fps is sharp enough for social platforms with smaller files and less upload data.

quiz.q: In CapCut, Mary wants to remove a 3-second pause in the middle of a clip. What should she do?
options: Split the clip at the start and end of the pause, then delete the middle part
Export at a higher frame rate
quiz.explain: Splitting at both points isolates the pause so she can delete only that part.

quiz.q: Roughly how many spoken words fit in a 30-second short video at a natural pace?
quiz.explain: At about 2 to 3 words per second, 30 seconds holds roughly 60 to 80 words.

quiz.q: Ifeoma's voiceover sounds echoey. She is recording in an empty tiled room. What is the best free fix?
options: Move to a room with soft furnishings like curtains, a bed or clothes
quiz.explain: Soft materials absorb sound reflections, reducing echo. Hard tiled rooms make it worse.

quiz.q: Insights show most viewers leave Joy's Reels in the first 3 seconds. What should she improve?
options: The call to action at the end
quiz.explain: Early drop-off means the opening did not grab attention. A stronger hook is the fix.

modules.title: Content Systems, AI, Photography and Distribution
modules.overview: Build a weekly content routine, use AI tools with a careful human check, take strong photos with natural light, and turn one piece of content into many while using only images you are allowed to use.

lessons.title: A weekly content system: pillars, calendar and batching
objectives: Define three to five content pillars for your business or group
Build a simple weekly content calendar
Batch create a week of posts in one or two sessions
Track what works with a simple results sheet

blocks.text: Most small businesses post when they remember, then go quiet for weeks. Customers forget them. A **content system** solves this: you decide in advance what kinds of things you post, when you post, and you make several posts at once. It turns content from a daily worry into a weekly routine of about two to three hours.

blocks.name: schedule
blocks.alt: A woman planning a schedule on a calendar
blocks.caption: A simple weekly plan replaces daily stress about what to post.

blocks.text: Step 1: Choose content pillars

**Content pillars** are the three to five main themes you post about again and again. They should match what your customers care about and what you sell. Rotating pillars keeps your feed varied without needing new ideas every day.

head: Pillar
Purpose
Example for a bakery
rows: Show what you sell and the price
How to store cake in hot weather
Show the people and the process

blocks.text: Step 2: Decide how often you can post

Be realistic. Posting three good times a week, every week, beats posting every day for one week and then stopping. A sensible start for a small business is **three feed posts or Reels a week** plus **daily WhatsApp Status** updates, which take less effort.
Step 3: Build a weekly calendar

A content calendar can be a simple table in a notebook, a Google Sheet, or the free notes app on your phone. Each row is a day, with columns for platform, pillar, format, idea, and status (planned, made, posted). Canva also has a **Content Planner** that lets you schedule posts to some social platforms; it is a Pro feature. Meta Business Suite, which is free, lets you schedule Facebook and Instagram posts in advance.

Plan around your real calendar too: market days, school resumption, salary week at month end, Ramadan and Sallah, Easter, Christmas and wedding seasons. Note these dates a month ahead so offers and posts are ready in time rather than rushed on the day.

blocks.title: A batching week
items: Sunday: plan ideas
Monday: shoot photos and clips
Tuesday: design and edit
Wed to Sat: post and reply
blocks.caption: Doing similar tasks together saves time and keeps posting steady.

blocks.text: Step 4: Batch create

**Batching** means doing the same type of task for many posts at once. Instead of planning, shooting, designing and posting one post every day, you plan all ideas in one sitting, take all photos in one session while the light is good, and design all graphics in one Canva session using your master templates. Batching works because you set up your light, props and app only once.

items: Shoot photos for several products in one daylight session, changing only the product.
Write all captions in one sitting and save them in a phone note.
Duplicate your Canva master templates for each post, then only swap photos and words.
Schedule posts in Meta Business Suite so they go out even on busy days.

blocks.text: Step 5: Track results

Once a week, spend ten minutes recording results in a simple sheet: date, post idea, pillar, reach or views, saves and shares, messages or enquiries, and sales you can link to it. After a month, look for patterns. Which pillar brings messages? Which format brings saves? Make more of what works and less of what does not.

Keep a simple **content bank**: a folder in your phone gallery for unused good photos and clips, and a note of captions you liked. On weeks when life is busy, you can post from the bank instead of going silent.

blocks.title: Worked example: a week planned for a small tailoring business
